prompt:
Create one landscape 3:2 Minecraft architectural MOOD BOARD on a plain warm light background. Title: "MARKETFRONT + HILLCLIMB" and subtitle "Pike Place Market / Seattle / 1.4 blocks per metre / Java 1.21.1". Crisp voxel style, actual vanilla Minecraft block geometry and textures only, no characters or animals (omit the pig sculpture to keep this constraint). Exterior architecture with only shallow lit shops visible behind glass. Dusk lighting on the models, warm glowing stalls and lanterns, neutral light sheet behind them.

Layout: upper half has THREE separate small complete-building isometric thumbnail studies, each showing the whole MarketFront complex and its adjacent hillclimb landing, each recognisably the same modern western Pike Place Market addition. Label them "01 / LONG GALLERY", "02 / STEPPED TERRACES", "03 / PLAZA + OVERLOOK". Vary emphasis in massing, flat roof tiers and timber canopy arrangements without changing site orientation or inventing pitched roofs. Lower left has FOUR large crisp detail callouts, labelled "TIMBER EAVE", "LIT GLASS GALLERY", "PLAZA EDGE", "HILLCLIMB TOWER". Bottom has a generous block palette strip grouped by WALLS, TRIM, ROOF, WINDOWS, ACCENTS. Print exact readable block ids underneath individual swatches, with minecraft: namespace, splitting labels into two lines if needed: WALLS minecraft:light_gray_concrete and minecraft:white_bricks is NOT valid, so use minecraft:quartz_bricks instead; TRIM minecraft:stripped_spruce_log and minecraft:spruce_planks; ROOF minecraft:smooth_stone_slab; WINDOWS minecraft:glass_pane; ACCENTS minecraft:polished_andesite, minecraft:lantern, minecraft:grass_block. Display only these nine valid ids, never the invalid white_bricks example. Use quartz brick texture for the old white masonry.

Essential architecture: a broad public rooftop plaza at uphill Pike Place level, light stone paving alternating with spruce decking, linear planters with grasses, benches, glass safety railings and open western bay views. Under that plaza, several exposed lower storeys stair-step down the steep bluff to the west, long horizontal glass-fronted market stalls and shops, warm timber posts and deep projecting timber eaves, gray metal-like concrete panels and exposed concrete retaining bases. Include a long transparent gallery, a restrained housing volume above with repeated balconies, and older white masonry market buildings with regular many-window elevations at the north end. Hillclimb: broad terraced concrete stairs and switchback ramps, grass planters between landings, benches, lantern lamps, a slim concrete-and-glass elevator/stair tower rising to the market.

Orientation must remain consistent across every thumbnail: west = low x = downhill = Elliott Bay, east = high x = uphill = Pike Place then 1st Avenue; north-west end = low z, Pike Street end = high z. Show views from the west/southwest exposing the stacked downhill facades and the rooftop plaza. Add a small orientation key "W / BAY / LOW x" and "E / PIKE PLACE / HIGH x", with z arrow labelled "PIKE STREET / +z". The hillclimb landing occupies the western adjacent plot and climbs east toward MarketFront. Preserve the irregular elongated north-south MarketFront site and irregular tapering hillclimb site as grounded terraced bases; no floating buildings, no buried facades, no rectangular invented platform beyond the site. Reference build envelopes: MarketFront 128 x 340 blocks with real roof around local y69; hillclimb 81 x133 blocks with tower roof around local y71. Ground climbs sharply east beneath MarketFront, exposing extra western storeys. These are concept thumbnails within the supplied irregular footprint constraints, not construction drawings. No extra iconic red Public Market sign, no skyline, no water backdrop, no invented neon. All render geometry must look buildable in Minecraft 1.21.1, no pale oak or later blocks, no smooth nonvoxel curves, no photoreal materials. Clear refined architectural sheet hierarchy with ample whitespace and legible lettering.
reads: Broad rooftop public plaza with pale paving, timber decking, benches, planters and glass railings.
Stacked downhill storeys exposing long bands of warmly lit market glazing.
Deep timber eaves and substantial spruce posts framing the shopfronts.
Gray panel walls and tall retaining bases grounding the complex on the bluff.
Flat roofs and stepped terraces, with recessed bays and upper balconies.
Older white masonry market buildings with repeated window grids behind the modern addition.
Broad hillclimb stairs broken into landscaped landings with lanterns.
Tall concrete-and-glass elevator and stair tower connecting the terraces.
